title: Those who love
hookLine: Guru Gobind Singh: only those who love find the Lord (Tav-Prasad Savaiye)
carry: wealth can be held without love

cards: Kings on elephants hung with gold. Armies in polished armor, horses dancing. Ascetics who've stood in cold rivers and gone without food.

Pilgrims who've bathed at every holy place. A Sikh hymn walks you through a procession like that. Then, after all that spectacle, the poet stops and says, in effect: I tell you the truth, all of you, listen.
Only those who love have found the Lord. The poet is Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru.

teach.b: The verses are the Tav-Prasad Savaiye, by Guru Gobind Singh, part of Nitnem, the Sikh daily prayers said in the morning. They look at power, wealth and hard religious effort, one after another.
Then comes the line the whole hymn leans on.
In the original, in the old Braj language written in Gurmukhi, it begins sach kahon, I speak the truth. Then, in paraphrase: listen, everyone, only those who have loved have found the Lord.
Jin prem kio, those who loved, tin hi prabh paio, they alone found God. The word for love there is prem.
Notice what the line doesn't say. It doesn't call kings and ascetics bad, or mock pilgrimage. It says none of those, by itself, is the thing.
Wealth can be held without love. Even fasting and cold baths can be done without love. The measure is not what you did, but whether you loved.

And this love isn't soft. Guru Gobind Singh is remembered as a warrior-saint, who founded the Khalsa and stood against tyranny: a leader who knew armies firsthand, telling everyone that armies aren't what finds God.
In Sikh teaching, love is the way to God, and it shows in remembering God's name, honest work and sharing with others.

how: Sikhs recite the Tav-Prasad Savaiye as part of Nitnem, the daily morning prayers, and the verses are also recited when the Khalsa initiation is given.

games.q: you've watched kings, armies and ascetics pass in the hymn. what does the Guru say finds the Lord?
games.why: after all the spectacle: I speak the truth, listen everyone, only those who have loved have found the Lord.

practice: Choose one thing to love with your whole heart, a person, the breath, the light in the room, the simple fact of being alive, and give it everything until the bell.
When your mind drifts to plans or worries, the parade going by, come back to the one thing; loving here means returning. If you pray, you can bring a name of God from your own tradition into this.

wordCard.voice: Prem. The word Guru Gobind Singh uses for love in the Tav-Prasad Savaiye: only those who have it have found the Lord. Today's word.

orig.note: Gurmukhi script (the savaiye are in Braj): love, the word in jin prem kio, those who loved.

carryVoice: Your line: wealth can be held without love. The Guru's measure is whether you loved. Day eight hundred forty-five.
